title: Finance Director Stole $3.9M from Bay Area Housing Fund, Got 1 Year in Prison
subtitle: Clarke Howatt — ABAG Housing Embezzlement
description: A source-backed examination of Clarke Howatt's embezzlement of nearly $3.9 million from the Association of Bay Area Governments, the restitution payment that recovered most but not all of it, and what a sentence built around a fast, well-resourced restitution payment reveals about how the federal system weighs repayment against the scale of a public-sector theft.
keyPoints: Embezzled nearly $3.9 million from the Association of Bay Area Governments between 2011-2015, affecting affordable housing developments including Rincon Hill highrise and Windemere Ranch housing projects
Sentenced to one year and one day in federal prison, six months of home confinement, and three years of supervised release.
He and his family paid $3.5 million in restitution — most, but not all, of the amount taken.
investigativeAngles: How a fast, well-resourced restitution payment shapes a federal sentence under 18 U.S.C. § 3553(a), separate from the legal requirement to make restitution at all.
What internal financial controls (separation of duties, independent audits) a public agency needs to catch a single-administrator embezzlement sooner.
guestOpportunities: a former prosecutor or defense attorney
an investigative reporter who covered the case
factCheckLayers: Published: Palo Alto Online - 2016; Bay Area News Group; Federal Court Records
